correctness.rationale: Each vertex coordinate is an integer-affine expression in q. Multiaffinity of the determinant makes a vertex-supported maximizer sufficient. Full signed-permutation transitivity reduces all unordered 4-tuples to 16215 anchored triples, checked by exact integer coefficient arithmetic from CHECK.py; each coefficient obeys (16,48,64,32) and one anchored triple attains all bounds with coherent sign. Since q>0, this proves a sharp bound uniformly for all real q>0, with exactly twelve orbit maximizers. Their vertex sets partition all 48 vertices; consequently any maximizing functional with three fixed vertices exposes a unique vertex, excluding all nonvertex maxima. A direct support-function equality with a 9-generator zonotope, its determinant-minor formula and exact computed minor sums establish the ambient volume. The rational derivative simplifies to the stated quartic and Descartes rule gives exactly one positive root and a global minimum.

originality.rationale: The nearest examined works study regular or similarity-constrained inner polyhedra, free spherical configurations, general simplex algorithms, ambient Archimedean-solid measurements, or an unrelated cube-octahedron intersection family. None of their inspected statements implies the 48-vertex full-parameter tetrahedral formula, unique anchored determinant extremum, disjoint partition of all vertices, or ratio minimum. Direct mathematical-alias and comparable-problem searches returned no matching theorem; historical priority remains provisional rather than guaranteed.

value.rationale: The q>0 family gives a natural continuous full-dimensional deformation from a cube toward a type-B3 root-zonotope with the regular truncated cuboctahedron as a distinguished interior member. The result settles unrestricted simplex optimality uniformly over this entire parameter family, gives a rigid 12-piece partition of all vertices into optimizer tetrahedra, and reveals a nontrivial unique best relative approximation regime. The sharply determined tetrahedral fraction in the regular Archimedean solid is a useful concrete benchmark; a single fixed example is not the motivation. This is not entailed by known ambient-volume tables, vertex enumeration alone, or a trivial monotone comparison.
